title: The exterior derivative squares to zero in a smooth chart
statement: Use the usual real and complex fields $\mathbf R$ and $\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $E$ and $F$ be real normed vector spaces, let $k\geq0$, let $x\in E$, and let $\omega:E\to\operatorname{Alt}^k_{\mathrm{cont},\mathbf R}(E,F)$ be a differential form which is $C^\infty$ at $x$. Here $\operatorname{Alt}^k_{\mathrm{cont},\mathbf R}(E,F)$ denotes the space of continuous alternating real $k$-linear maps from $E^k$ to $F$, and $d\omega$ is the alternation of the Fréchet derivative of $\omega$. Then $(d(d\omega))(x)=0$. In particular $F$ may be $\mathbf C$ regarded as a real normed vector space.
